summary: A finite, exact-weight fragment of compositional Bayesian semantics: a model is a finite list of configurations with rational weights and observation is conditioning. What the hypotheses entail has probability 1; probability is monotone along entailment; two observations in sequence are one joint observation; the literal listener of RSA.v is conditioning on truth; with equal weights the two printed forms of the generalized quantifier agree; and 'many' and 'most' make the corresponding instance probable above their thresholds. A worked chair model has exact values 1/2, 2/3 and 1/3.

sources.citation: Bernardy, J.-P., Blanck, R., Chatzikyriakidis, S. & Lappin, S. (2018). A Compositional Bayesian Semantics for Natural Language. Proc. First International Workshop on Language Cognition and Computational Models, pp. 1-10 (ACL Anthology W18-4101).
sources.available: not in the corpus; read from the public ACL Anthology copy

theorems.name: B1_entailed_is_certain
theorems.source_claim: B1_entailed_is_certain. What is entailed by the hypotheses is certain. modelSimple of sec. 2.1 is the case A = H.

theorems.name: B2_monotone
theorems.source_claim: B2_monotone. Probability is monotone along entailment.

theorems.name: B3_complement
theorems.source_claim: B3_complement. A sentence and its negation share the unit.

theorems.name: B4_chain
theorems.source_claim: B4_chain. Two observations in sequence are one joint observation.

theorems.name: B5_literal_listener_is_conditioning
theorems.source_claim: B5_literal_listener_is_conditioning. The bridge. The RSA literal listener, summed over a set of worlds, is the probability of that set given that the utterance is true.

theorems.name: B6_uniform_is_counting
theorems.source_claim: B6_uniform_is_counting. With equal weights on individuals, eq. (2) is eq. (1): a ratio of cardinalities.

theorems.name: B7_quantifier_supports_instance
theorems.source_claim: B7_quantifier_supports_instance. The prediction of sec. 2.4: "if many chairs have four legs, then it is likely that any given chair has four legs". Here "likely" is: more probable than the quantifier's threshold.

theorems.name: E1_many_has_mass_half
theorems.source_claim: "Many chairs have four legs" holds in one configuration of the two.

theorems.name: E2_before_observing
theorems.source_claim: Before the observation, a chair has four legs with probability 1/2.

theorems.name: B8_supported_not_entailed_and_inverse_fails
theorems.source_claim: B8. Separation, on this model. The supported instance is not entailed: its probability is below 1. And the inverse inference is not supported by the semantics alone: here it is below 1/2. [BBCL18] reports 0.653 for the inverse under its...

evidence: DRAFT for the author's review; not an accepted source-level verdict.
The paper's priors are Gaussian and its numbers are sampling estimates; the file uses finite models with exact rational weights and does not reproduce those numbers.
Comparatives, vague predicates and learning (sections 2.2, 2.3, 3) are not formalized.

determination_rationale: DRAFT for the author. A finite analogue of the paper's semantics, not the paper's continuous model.

artifact_classes.description: finite lists of configurations with rational weights in place of vector spaces with Gaussian priors

notes: Builds on RSA.v, which it leaves unchanged. Not yet cross-reviewed. No survey entry is linked to this file. DRAFT RECORD: the faithfulness verdict, the determination and the assessment status are the author's to set.
